openings.claim: Prevent inconsistent storage addresses by checking the reserved reader's surname when shelving and updating the behind-desk exception slip immediately whenever a book changes location.
openings.delta: Divider cards still narrow shelf searches, but household surnames are rejected as placement keys. Replace the once-before-opening exception snapshot with move-time pencil corrections; keep cart arrivals retrievable without compulsory shelving.
openings.prediction: If inconsistent addresses cause repeated searches, checking placement and maintaining current exceptions will reduce second-location searches and retrieval time, including during the concentrated arrival interval. This remains a proposed effect, not an observed benefit.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is that queue congestion dominates delays. Correct addresses would then reduce searching but leave the fraction finishing within two minutes below 95% during the burst.
openings.defeat: An evening with verified correct addresses and current exceptions still has more than 5% of available-hold pickups exceeding two minutes; any wrong-reader handoff or preparation above ten clerk-minutes also defeats qualification for the original task.
openings.probe: Run one bounded evening trial using existing paper, pencils, divider cards, shelves, cart and timing sheet. The existing clerk performs all handoffs. Keep identifying records behind the desk. Cap daily preparation at ten clerk-minutes; record move-correction time, second searches, arrival-to-handoff time and identity-check failures. Compare burst and quieter encounters. If preparation cannot finish within the cap, stop preparation and record failure rather than extend it.
assumptions: A reliable reserved-reader identity is accessible for each book; this is unconfirmed.
Placement checking and move-time updates may fit available clerk time, but O6 does not establish that capability.
The bounded probe preserves the stated resource and privacy limits; the eventual intervention's throughput and correctness remain unproven.
